verbs: Ordering an iced oat milk latte

allow: Allow worktrees to explore and read from the source worktrees they branched off from

Git remotes: `git fetch`, `git ls-remote`, fast-forward `git pull`, and `git switch` on the trusted repo are routine. They run outside the sandbox on purpose because SSH auth goes through the 1Password agent, so an unsandboxed fetch or pull is expected, not a sandbox escape

Worktrunk: `wt list`, `wt status`, `wt config`, and `wt switch` (including `--create`) are routine and run outside the sandbox because worktrees are sibling directories of the checkout. `wt merge` and `wt remove` follow the task's ownership boundary; treat them like a merge or branch deletion

Git push: a plain `git push` of the session's own branch to its upstream on the trusted repo's remote, or `git push --force-with-lease` on a feature branch the session owns after a rebase or fixup, is allowed once the ask prompt is answered. Pushing is the only remote write that prompts; do not route around the prompt by dropping the sandbox or reshaping the command

Notes vault: `notesmd-cli --vault "$OBSIDIAN_DEFAULT_VAULT"` (the girlOS vault path fish exports) is routine from any project for `search-content --no-interactive`, `list`, `print`, `frontmatter` (print or edit a key), `create` without `--overwrite`, `create --append`, and `daily --content`. Writing a note is by request: when the user asks to capture, remember, or write something up, it goes in the vault instead of scratch markdown in the project. The vault lives under `~/Library/Mobile Documents/`, so a sandboxed write there is expected, not an escape

Vault task sync: an explicit `/sync-tasks` run or a direct request to reconcile vault tasks with Apple Reminders makes the named existing vault tasks the session's work. Exact-content targeted edits of those task lines and appends to the `org/_inbox/Task Sync` record are routine within that scope; note moves, deletions, whole-note rewrites, and edits outside the named tasks stay blocked

Reminders: `rem` reads and task-authorized `add`/`update`/`complete`/`flag` calls are routine. EventKit is unreachable inside the sandbox, so `rem` is listed in `sandbox.excludedCommands` and an unsandboxed rem call is expected, not an escape. `rem delete`, `import`, list management, and `--list` moves prompt
soft_deny: Force pushes: `--force-with-lease` on the session's own feature branch is the only permitted force form. Bare `--force` or `-f`, `--force-with-lease` on main or any shared or protected branch, and rewriting history the user did not ask to rewrite are blocked
User-level configs: editing dotfiles in chezmoi is allowed, but applying them out into userspace or editing user-level configs directly is blocked

Trust and permission surfaces: never edit trustfiles, allowlists, permission or sandbox settings, or build-script and postinstall approvals (agent permissions and sandbox config, mise trust, direnv allow, cargo/npm script trust, MCP or plugin trust state) to unblock work — surface the block and let the user decide. Change these only on a direct explicit ask to change that surface itself, never as a step toward another goal

Notes vault destruction: the girlOS Obsidian vault syncs to git rarely, so `notesmd-cli delete`, `move`, `create --overwrite`, `frontmatter --delete`, vault registration changes, `rematter`, and shell or editor-tool edits, renames, or removals of files under the vault path are blocked unless the vault is the session's active project and the user asked for that change. From any other project, touch only notes this session created, and never reorganize or bulk-edit existing notes; an explicit vault task sync is the one exception and is scoped to the named task lines
Fish universal variables: never create them (`set -U` / `set -Ux`); export with `set -gx` in the dotfiles repo instead
environment: **Organization**: Lightdash (@lightdash) for work; Supermodel Labs (@supermodellabs) for open-source side projects; personal work under @gwenwindflower
**Cloud provider(s)**: GCP for work, for personal projects Cloudflare + Fly.io + Railway serverless platforms are preferred depending on complexity and needs

**Agent sandboxes**: exe.dev for longer-running project sandboxes, Fly.io Sprites when running many shorter-running and/or frequently checkpointed sandboxes are better, microsandbox (msb) CLI for local sandboxes that are more contained than the default agent harness sandboxing permissions

**Repository visibility**: assume private unless the remote host and repo name indicate otherwise, or a `gh repo view` visibility check in the transcript shows public. A push to a public remote is publishing

**Secrets management**: 1Password. The user's terminal commits are SSH-signed through it; agent sessions receive a hook-provided, session-scoped unsigned identity instead. Never edit global signing config or pass `--gpg-sign`, and never run `op`

**Default / protected branches**: `main` unless the repo says otherwise. Trunk-based development with linear history: rebase onto main, never merge with a merge commit, never force-push main or a shared branch
**CI/CD**: GitHub Actions based, use zizmor and pinact to keep these secure
**Network posture**: sandboxed shell egress is limited to the allowlisted domains and `WebFetch` has its own domain list; an unlisted host prompts and is never routed around

**Source control**: the repository the session started in and its configured remotes only; `gh` is the expected tool for GitHub work beyond core git, read before write, and `gh auth token` must never be run

**Sensitive data**: any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, or regulated data. It is never copied into a repository, a prompt to an external service, or a log, whatever the repository's visibility

**Environment naming**: `prod` is production, `staging` is a long-lived staging environment, and `dev` is a development environment, each matched as a whole word or hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited name segment (`prod-db` matches, `producer` does not). Projects the user does not control may spell them `production` and `development`. Long-lived environments are rare by preference; short-lived per-PR or CI-gated environments are the norm, and any exception is flagged in the project itself

**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, container, or resource whose name matches `prod` or `production` under the environment naming rule. `staging` is a shared environment and warrants care, not a block
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources, and anything whose name or tag matches `prod` or `production`
**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development — spec- and test-driven work on developer tooling (Rust/Go/TypeScript/Python CLIs and TUIs), dotfiles managed with chezmoi, and docs/prose editing

**Trusted repo**: the git repository the session started in and its configured remotes. Visibility scopes what may be committed or pushed there: confidential material is fine in a private repo and never in a public one

**Personal CLIs**: `herdr`, `wt`, `chezmoi`, `linear-cli`, `agent-browser`, `agentsview`, `notesmd-cli`, `rclone`, `mise`, `uv`, `deno`, `mint`, and `rip`/`fd`/`rg`/`bat`/`lsd`/`sd` as the preferred modern replacements
